headline: Instinct's assistant now phones businesses for early users, and Meta is testing the same for Muse.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: Instinct Concierge was announced 16 Sep 2026 and the Muse calling test rests on unnamed reports; the column adds context, not a new event.
importance_line: People can start handing routine phone calls to an AI agent, which saves time but hands software the power to agree to things in their name, and both companies' own terms warn that agent actions can be wrong and hard to undo.
summary: Fox News reports that Instinct, a well-funded personal-assistant startup valued at $10 billion after a $1 billion round on 28 Sep 2026, has opened early access to Concierge, announced 16 Sep 2026, which lets its agent call restaurants, clinics and service providers on a user's behalf, and that Meta is reportedly testing a similar outbound-calling feature for some users of its Muse agent. The column stresses the trade-off: Instinct's own terms say agent actions can be incorrect and not always reversible, and both services gain access to messages, accounts and payment details once connected.
notes: Read at the AMP mirror noticias.foxnews.com; url points at the canonical foxnews.com path. Muse calling attributed by Fox News to unnamed reports.
